title: Detached read-only capture window drops all terminal colors
existing_state: When a capture step detaches (timeout/Ctrl+C/max-lines/natural completion) the window stays open showing a history snapshot, but RenderDetachedHistorySnapshot rebuilds it from the plain-text transcript and fills every cell with the default gray-on-black (Forms/InteractiveTerminalForm.cs:607-610: Array.Fill with single fore/back colors) — syntax-colored device output, diff colors, and alarm highlighting that were on screen one frame earlier all flatten to monochrome the instant the step detaches.
recommendation: Instead of re-rendering from the text transcript, capture the last live TerminalScreenSnapshot stream: have the service build the detached view from the Rebex screen + history cells (the same per-cell color path BuildScreenSnapshot already implements at InteractiveTerminalService.cs:3333-3469) at detach time, falling back to the monochrome text path only when no snapshot exists (e.g., headless capture promoted to a window).
user_benefit: The post-detach review window — the whole point of leaving it open — keeps the color cues (errors in red, status in green) that operators actually scan for.

evidence.note: Detached snapshot fills uniform default fore/back colors for every cell
BuildScreenSnapshot already produces per-cell colored snapshots that could seed the detached view

mockup_idea: Side-by-side: live capture window with colored 'show interfaces' output vs. the current detached view of the same content in flat gray; the 'after' shows the detached view retaining colors with the 'Detached (read-only)' title.
